depth: The depth map depicts the three-dimensional layout of a living-room corner. A television on a stand is positioned approximately 2.5 to 3 metres directly ahead against the left wall. It is bordered by a taller shelf about 2 metres away and 1 metre to the TV's left, plus a smaller shelf around 3.5 metres away in the dark rear corner, 1 metre to the TV's right. Nearer the camera wearer, a round ottoman at the lower-left and a low coffee table beside the right wall are roughly 1 to 1.5 metres away, with toy blocks lying between them on the floor at about 1.5 metres. At that point, a blue-clad person and a raised left hand enter the lower-right foreground at under 0.5 metres, placing them well within the camera wearer's arm's reach and each other's reach. They partially block the sofa and coffee table behind them as the left shelf leaves the view. The person at the extreme right is strongly cropped by the image edge and seems turned sideways toward the left—toward either the TV or camera wearer—instead of looking straight into the lens. Compared with RGB alone, the map more clearly shows the uninterrupted depth gradient across the right wall, floor, and recessed ceiling, and distinctly separates the sub-metre foreground person and sofa from furniture 2 to 3 metres away. However, it is unreliable around the wall clock, which disappears into the flat wall surface, and within the open shelf cubbies, whose depth edges become blurred.
segmentation: Across the five-frame pan to the right, the instance-segmentation map separates several individual room objects. It repeatedly detects the television screen 2.5 to 3 metres ahead, the potted plant on the upper-left corner of the left shelf about 2 metres away and slightly higher than the TV, the circular wall clock above the television except in frames 3 and 5, and the low right-side table at a distance of 1 to 1.5 metres. As the camera turns right in frame 5, the map segments the partially shown person in blue together with the nearby foreground hand and arm in the bottom-right corner, all within 0.5 metres and therefore within the arm's reach of both the camera wearer and one another. Their foreground masks overlap and partly cover the green table mask behind them. Although segmentation draws sharp two-dimensional boundaries around the television, plant, and table and separates these objects from the surrounding clutter, its semantic labels and spatial interpretation are very unreliable in this scene. It entirely fails to detect the shelves, floor toys, ottoman, and sofa. The right coffee table is inconsistently classified as a 'bed' in frame 1 and a 'dining table' in frames 2, 4, and 5, while being absent in frame 3; the fruit bowl on it is also mislabeled as 'pizza' in frame 4. In addition, cartoon characters and an eagle shown on the flat television display 2.5 to 3 metres away are wrongly segmented as genuine 'person' instances in frames 2 through 5, producing false-positive figures that seem to face into the room.
pose: Frames 1 through 4 of the body-and-hand skeleton map are entirely empty, confirming that no actual people appear during the initial fixed view toward the television and shelving located 2 to 3.5 metres away. When the camera wearer turns right in frame 5, one yellow upper-body and arm skeleton segment emerges in the bottom-right corner. It corresponds to the blue-shirted person situated within 0.5 metres of the wearer—inside arm's reach—and approximately 1.5 metres in front of the coffee table. This skeletal link runs diagonally from the right edge downward toward the lower-right, showing that the person's torso and arm extend leftward across the lower foreground instead of facing the camera head-on. Most of the person's body and head remain cut off beyond the right frame border. In contrast to the segmentation output, the pose detector successfully disregards the two-dimensional cartoon figures displayed on the TV 2.5 to 3 metres away and identifies only the real person in the foreground of frame 5. Nevertheless, its frame-5 result is mostly unreliable: severe cropping at the edge and the person's close range prevent it from capturing the complete torso and head direction. It also entirely misses the magenta hand skeleton for the visibly open hand located within arm's reach at the bottom-right beside the person.
